title: Transport normalized lax structures and their mates across monoidal equivalences
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal A',\mathcal B'$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Let $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ and $F:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$ be fully faithful essentially surjective functors with specified strong monoidal structures [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $L:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:R$ and $L':\mathcal A'\rightleftarrows\mathcal B':R'$ be specified adjunctions, and let $\beta:ER\cong R'F$ and $\gamma:FL\cong L'E$ be natural isomorphisms identifying the adjunctions, including their units and counits [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Equivalently, for $h:LX\to Y$ the Hom bijections $\Phi,\Phi'$ satisfy $\beta_Y E(\Phi(h))=\Phi'(F(h)\gamma_X^{-1})$. Give $R'$ a lax monoidal structure. Then there is a unique lax monoidal structure on $R$ making $\beta$ monoidal relative to the specified structures of $E,F$. Under $\gamma$, its left-adjoint oplax mate maps are the transported mate maps for $L'\dashv R'$, including the unit. In particular, if those tensor and unit mate maps for $L'$ are invertible, so are the corresponding maps for $L$. Here lax and oplax structures and their mates have the conventions of [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate].

source.place: Tag 001J (definition-equivalence-categories), for the equivalence setting; agent extraction of full-faithful monoidal transport, using the mate formulas of Mathlib CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean:1064–1066.

proof.text:
Write $p_{U,V},a$ for the tensor and unit isomorphisms of $E$, and $q_{Y,Z},b$ for those of $F$, with orientations as in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Write $m',e'$ for the given lax structure of $R'$. Throughout, juxtaposition means composition with the rightmost map first. Put $K=R'F$ and define
$$n_{Y,Z}=R'(q_{Y,Z})m'_{FY,FZ},\qquad v=R'(b)e'.$$
These have domains $KY\otimes KZ$ and $\mathbf1_{\mathcal A'}$, respectively. For maps $f:Y\to Y'$, $g:Z\to Z'$, naturality of $q$ and $m'$ gives
$$K(f\otimes g)n_{Y,Z}=R'(q_{Y',Z'})m'_{FY',FZ'}(Kf\otimes Kg)=n_{Y',Z'}(Kf\otimes Kg).$$

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category), 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent calculation with the displayed coherence identities.

proof.text:
Check associativity of these particular maps $n$. Expanding its left side and moving $R'(q_{Y,Z})$ through $m'$ by naturality gives
$$K(\alpha^{\mathcal B})n_{Y\otimes Z,W}(n_{Y,Z}\otimes1)=R'\bigl(F(\alpha^{\mathcal B})q_{Y\otimes Z,W}(q_{Y,Z}\otimes1)\bigr)m'_{FY\otimes FZ,FW}(m'_{FY,FZ}\otimes1).$$
The strong associativity equation for $F$ replaces the expression inside $R'$ by $q_{Y,Z\otimes W}(1\otimes q_{Z,W})\alpha^{\mathcal B'}$. The lax associativity equation for $R'$ then replaces $R'(\alpha^{\mathcal B'})m'_{FY\otimes FZ,FW}(m'_{FY,FZ}\otimes1)$ by $m'_{FY,FZ\otimes FW}(1\otimes m'_{FZ,FW})\alpha^{\mathcal A'}$. Moving $R'(1\otimes q_{Z,W})$ back through $m'$ yields exactly
$$n_{Y,Z\otimes W}(1\otimes n_{Z,W})\alpha^{\mathcal A'}_{KY,KZ,KW}.$$
This is the required associativity equation, using only the specified axioms.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category), 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent calculation with the displayed coherence identities.

proof.text:
The two unit equations for $n,v$ follow by these expansions, with the unitors carrying their indicated category superscripts:
$$\begin{aligned}
K(\lambda^{\mathcal B}_Y)n_{\mathbf1,Y}(v\otimes1)&=R'\bigl(F(\lambda^{\mathcal B}_Y)q_{\mathbf1,Y}(b\otimes1)\bigr)m'_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal B'},FY}(e'\otimes1)\\
&=R'(\lambda^{\mathcal B'}_{FY})m'_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal B'},FY}(e'\otimes1)=\lambda^{\mathcal A'}_{KY},\\
K(\rho^{\mathcal B}_Y)n_{Y,\mathbf1}(1\otimes v)&=R'\bigl(F(\rho^{\mathcal B}_Y)q_{Y,\mathbf1}(1\otimes b)\bigr)m'_{FY,\mathbf1_{\mathcal B'}}(1\otimes e')\\
&=R'(\rho^{\mathcal B'}_{FY})m'_{FY,\mathbf1_{\mathcal B'}}(1\otimes e')=\rho^{\mathcal A'}_{KY}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality in each line uses naturality of $m'$, the second uses the corresponding unit equation for $F$, and the last uses that of $R'$. Thus $n,v$ are a lax structure on $K$.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category), 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent calculation with the displayed coherence identities.

proof.text:
Put $H=ER$ and set
$$k_{Y,Z}=\beta_{Y\otimes Z}^{-1}n_{Y,Z}(\beta_Y\otimes\beta_Z),\qquad w=\beta_{\mathbf1}^{-1}v.$$
These are natural: for $f:Y\to Y'$, $g:Z\to Z'$, substitution and naturality of $\beta,n$ give $H(f\otimes g)k_{Y,Z}=k_{Y',Z'}(Hf\otimes Hg)$. They satisfy coherence by direct cancellation. Specifically, postcomposing the two sides of the associativity equation for $k$ with $\beta_{Y\otimes(Z\otimes W)}$ reduces them to
$$K(\alpha^{\mathcal B})n_{Y\otimes Z,W}(n_{Y,Z}\otimes1)((\beta_Y\otimes\beta_Z)\otimes\beta_W)$$
and
$$n_{Y,Z\otimes W}(1\otimes n_{Z,W})\alpha^{\mathcal A'}((\beta_Y\otimes\beta_Z)\otimes\beta_W),$$
using naturality of $\beta$ and the associator. These agree by Step 2. Postcomposing the left and right unit equations with $\beta_Y$ gives respectively $K(\lambda^{\mathcal B})n_{\mathbf1,Y}(v\otimes\beta_Y)=\beta_Y\lambda^{\mathcal A'}_{HY}$ and $K(\rho^{\mathcal B})n_{Y,\mathbf1}(\beta_Y\otimes v)=\beta_Y\rho^{\mathcal A'}_{HY}$, which follow from Step 3 and naturality of the unitors. Cancellation of $\beta$ proves the equations for $k,w$.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category), 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent calculation with the displayed coherence identities.

proof.text:
Full faithfulness means that every map between objects $EU,EV$ has exactly one inverse image under $E$. Define $m_{Y,Z}:RY\otimes RZ\to R(Y\otimes Z)$ and $e:\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}\to R\mathbf1_{\mathcal B}$ by
$$E(m_{Y,Z})=k_{Y,Z}p_{RY,RZ}^{-1},\qquad E(e)=wa^{-1}.$$
The displayed arrows have exactly the required image domains and codomains, so fullness supplies them. To check naturality apply $E$ to $R(f\otimes g)m_{Y,Z}=m_{Y',Z'}(Rf\otimes Rg)$ and precompose with $p_{RY,RZ}$. Naturality of $p$ turns this into $H(f\otimes g)k_{Y,Z}=k_{Y',Z'}(Hf\otimes Hg)$, proved in Step 4. Since $p$ is invertible and $E$ is faithful, the desired equation holds.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category), 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent calculation with the displayed coherence identities.

proof.text:
Check all three coherences for $m,e$ by the same explicit substitutions. For associativity apply $E$ and precompose both sides with
$$t=p_{RY\otimes RZ,RW}(p_{RY,RZ}\otimes1).$$
Naturality and associativity of $p$ turn the left side into $H(\alpha^{\mathcal B})k_{Y\otimes Z,W}(k_{Y,Z}\otimes1)$ and the right side into $k_{Y,Z\otimes W}(1\otimes k_{Z,W})\alpha^{\mathcal A'}_{HY,HZ,HW}$. These agree by Step 4. For left unitality, apply $E$ and precompose with $p_{\mathbf1,RY}(a\otimes1)$: naturality of $p$ and its left unit equation reduce the two sides to $H(\lambda^{\mathcal B})k_{\mathbf1,Y}(w\otimes1)$ and $\lambda^{\mathcal A'}_{HY}$. For right unitality precompose instead with $p_{RY,\mathbf1}(1\otimes a)$, obtaining $H(\rho^{\mathcal B})k_{Y,\mathbf1}(1\otimes w)$ and $\rho^{\mathcal A'}_{HY}$. Step 4 gives both equalities. Cancel these isomorphisms and use faithfulness. Thus $m,e$ are lax monoidal. Their defining equations are precisely
$$\beta_{Y\otimes Z}E(m_{Y,Z})p_{RY,RZ}=R'(q_{Y,Z})m'_{FY,FZ}(\beta_Y\otimes\beta_Z),\qquad \beta_{\mathbf1}E(e)a=R'(b)e',$$
so $\beta$ is monoidal. Conversely these two equations force the displayed values of $E(m),E(e)$; faithfulness forces $m,e$ themselves, proving uniqueness.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category), 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent calculation with the displayed coherence identities.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate] to the lax structure just constructed and to the given lax structure on $R'$. Write $u,u'$ for the adjunction units, and $d_{X,Y},d_0$ and $d'_{U,V},d'_0$ for the resulting oplax maps. The cited statement supplies their coherence and their actual transposes
$$\Phi(d_{X,Y})=m_{LX,LY}(u_X\otimes u_Y),\quad \Phi(d_0)=e,$$
with the analogous primed formulas. Use the specified Hom-bijection compatibility in the item (with the mate convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]), at $h=1_{LX}$. Naturality of $\Phi'$ in its target gives the exact unit comparison
$$\beta_{LX}E(u_X)=\Phi'(\gamma_X^{-1})=R'(\gamma_X^{-1})u'_{EX}.$$
This uses the given comparison of adjunctions, rather than choosing a new adjunction for either underlying functor.

source.place: Agent calculation from the specified comparison of adjunctions; mate formulas in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean:1064-1066, as stated in lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate.

proof.text:
For $X,Y\in\mathcal A$, let
$$s_{X,Y}=q_{LX,LY}(\gamma_X^{-1}\otimes\gamma_Y^{-1}):L'EX\otimes L'EY\longrightarrow F(LX\otimes LY).$$
It is invertible. The monoidality equation from Step 6, naturality of $p$, and the unit comparison from Step 7 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{LX\otimes LY}E\bigl(m_{LX,LY}(u_X\otimes u_Y)\bigr)
&=R'(q_{LX,LY})m'_{FLX,FLY}\bigl(\beta_{LX}E(u_X)\otimes\beta_{LY}E(u_Y)\bigr)p_{X,Y}^{-1}\\
&=R'(s_{X,Y})m'_{L'EX,L'EY}(u'_{EX}\otimes u'_{EY})p_{X,Y}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is naturality of $m'$ for the two arrows $\gamma_X^{-1},\gamma_Y^{-1}$; all maps have domain $E(X\otimes Y)$ and codomain $R'F(LX\otimes LY)$.

source.place: Agent calculation with the mate tensor formula, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean:1066.

proof.text:
By the specified Hom compatibility, the left side of Step 8 is $\Phi'(F(d_{X,Y})\gamma_{X\otimes Y}^{-1})$. By naturality in both variables of the primed Hom bijection and the primed tensor-mate formula in [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate], its right side is
$$\Phi'\bigl(s_{X,Y}d'_{EX,EY}L'(p_{X,Y}^{-1})\bigr).$$
Injectivity of that bijection therefore proves the exact tensor transport identity
$$F(d_{X,Y})=q_{LX,LY}(\gamma_X^{-1}\otimes\gamma_Y^{-1})d'_{EX,EY}L'(p_{X,Y}^{-1})\gamma_{X\otimes Y}.$$
This is precisely the tensor comparison for $L'$ transported under the specified strong structures and $\gamma$; no tensor comparison is identified merely up to an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Agent calculation with the mate tensor formula, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean:1066.

proof.text:
For the unit, the defining equation in Step 6 gives
$$\beta_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal B}}E(e)=R'(b)e'a^{-1}.$$
The Hom compatibility and the unit-mate formulas in [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate] turn this into
$$\Phi'\bigl(F(d_0)\gamma_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}}^{-1}\bigr)=\Phi'\bigl(bd'_0L'(a^{-1})\bigr).$$
Both maps being transposed have domain $L'E\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}$ and codomain $F\mathbf1_{\mathcal B}$. Injectivity proves
$$F(d_0)=bd'_0L'(a^{-1})\gamma_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}}.$$
Thus the unit mate, as well as the tensor mate, is the transported specified mate.

source.place: Agent calculation with the mate unit formula, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean:1065.

proof.text: If $d'_{U,V}$ and $d'_0$ are invertible, each factor on the right sides of the identities in Steps 9 and 10 is invertible: this includes $L'(p^{-1}),L'(a^{-1})$, since applying a functor to a two-sided inverse gives a two-sided inverse. Hence $F(d_{X,Y})$ and $F(d_0)$ have inverses. For either arrow $z$, fullness of $F$ lifts $F(z)^{-1}$ to an arrow $z^*$; faithfulness applied to $F(z^*z)=1$ and $F(zz^*)=1$ gives $z^*z=1$ and $zz^*=1$. Therefore every $d_{X,Y}$ and $d_0$ is invertible. This also shows that no essential-surjectivity or strictness assumption was needed in the calculations beyond the hypotheses already given.

source.place: Agent two-sided-inverse calculation in the fully faithful setting of Tag 001J (definition-equivalence-categories).
